svg.title: Technique and breathing: a map with two axes
svg.desc: Schematic map with two axes, technique and breathing. The horizontal axis is how finely dose is shaped — 3D conformal, IMRT, rotational modulation, protons; the vertical axis holds one thing only, deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH). The axes are independent, and indication decides where a patient lands, not budget. The first cell, 3D conformal and IMRT (the NHI-covered standard technique), is filled with real figures rather than adjectives: modern mean heart dose for left-sided treatment averaged 5.4 Gy in literature published 2003 to 2013 and 3.6 Gy in literature published 2014 to 2017, with those published in 2017 averaging 2.6 Gy; measured across 4,687 patients at one institution, left-sided conventional fractionation (50 Gy in 25 fractions) had a median of 2.16 Gy and hypofractionation (42.6 Gy in 16 fractions) a median of 1.47 Gy; with respiratory control the literature average was 1.7 Gy against 4.5 Gy without, and tangential fields plus respiratory control 1.3 Gy; against the wedged and 2D technique of an earlier era, randomised trials showed moist desquamation 31.2% against 47.8%, 5-year change in breast appearance 40% against 58%, and an odds ratio of 0.68 for poor overall cosmesis. The second cell is rotational modulation, with VMAT and TOMO inside the same cell and no ranking between them: the differences that matter appear on complex targets — chest wall plus regional nodes especially the internal mammary chain, a reconstructed chest wall, synchronous bilateral treatment, difficult anatomy. In a Taiwanese comparison of 108 left-sided plans with regional nodal irradiation, mean heart dose was 3.82 Gy with VMAT against 5.13 Gy with TOMO, with lung and contralateral breast pointing the same way, so the two trade places depending on the situation and the planning; the cost is that helical delivery increases the low-dose bath to non-target volumes; no randomised comparison of clinical outcomes between TOMO and ordinary IMRT was found; the NHI schedule contains no TOMO-specific item and no official self-pay amount was found at any hospital. The third cell, protons: mean heart dose in the 0.5 Gy range without the internal mammary chain and 2.6 Gy with it, the lowest of any technique, with a 70-patient prospective series measuring 0.44 Gy to the whole heart; the randomised RADCOMP trial has completed accrual at 1,238 patients with major cardiovascular events as its primary endpoint and has not reported, the registry's estimated primary completion date being November 2036; protons carry their own costs, with rib fracture in 7% of a prospective cohort and 3.7% at 3 years in a 225-patient series (0.4% symptomatic), and no photon skin-sparing effect at the entrance so that skin dose depends on the planning; Taiwan's three NHI proton codes apply only to patients under nineteen, so proton therapy for adult breast cancer is entirely self-paid. The fourth row is DIBH: it layers onto 3D conformal, IMRT, VMAT or TOMO alike, reduces dose by roughly 20 to 70% varying from person to person (dosimetric), and after pre-selection and training about three in ten still cannot complete a breath-hold planning scan; the proton cell is the exception, where free breathing already gives 0.48 Gy and breath hold 0.31 Gy, a small marginal gain; the NHI schedule contains no respiratory-control or breath-hold item, and no official self-pay charge for photon breath hold was found at any hospital. A footnote records that side is not the only axis: mean heart dose averages 5.4 Gy on the left and 3.3 Gy on the right, and including the internal mammary chain doubles the typical heart dose.

g.text: TECHNIQUE × DIBH — A MAP, NOT A PRICE LIST
Technique and breathing: a map
with two axes
The horizontal axis is how finely dose is shaped: 3D conformal,
then IMRT, then rotational modulation, then protons. The vertical
axis holds one thing only — DIBH.
The axes are independent: which machine delivers the dose and
whether you hold your breath are two separate questions, and
indication decides where you land.
3D conformal
IMRT
Rotational: VMAT/TOMO
Protons
Dose conforms more closely along the axis — but closer does not win every
cell; each cell's conditions are set out below
Indication decides where you land, not budget
Tumour site, the volume to be treated and your own anatomy
decide the cell; price comes after those two questions. Where
no official schedule of charges exists, ask the hospital's
business office.
3D conformal / IMRT
NHI-covered standard technique
The current standard, not a stripped-down option —
this cell holds real numbers
Modern mean heart dose, left-sided: literature published 2003
to 2013 averaged 5.4 Gy; published 2014 to 2017, 3.6 Gy, and
among those published in 2017, 2.6 Gy.
Measured in a single institution across 4,687 patients:
left-sided conventional fractionation (50 Gy in 25 fractions)
median 2.16 Gy; hypofractionation (42.6 Gy in 16 fractions)
median 1.47 Gy.
With respiratory control: literature average 1.7 Gy against 4.5
Gy without; tangential fields plus respiratory control 1.3 Gy.
Randomised evidence (against the wedged and 2D technique of an
earlier era): moist desquamation 31.2% against 47.8%; 5-year
change in breast appearance 40% against 58%; odds ratio 0.68
for poor overall cosmesis.
Rotational: VMAT and TOMO
one cell, no ranking inside it
The differences that matter show up on complex targets
Where it counts: chest wall plus regional nodes (particularly
the internal mammary chain), a reconstructed chest wall,
synchronous bilateral treatment, difficult anatomy — rotational
delivery can hold coverage and homogeneity together
(dosimetric).
No ranking inside the cell: in a Taiwanese comparison of 108
left-sided plans with regional nodal irradiation, mean heart
dose was 3.82 Gy with VMAT against 5.13 Gy with TOMO, with lung
and contralateral breast pointing the same way — the two trade
places depending on the situation and the planning.
The cost is in the source text: helical delivery increases the
low-dose bath to non-target volumes.
Between TOMO and ordinary IMRT, no randomised comparison of
clinical outcomes was found; what can be compared is dose
distribution and retrospective data.
The NHI schedule contains no TOMO-specific item, and no
official published self-pay amount was found at any hospital —
ask the business office.
Protons
referral / fully self-paid in adults
Dosimetrically clear; the randomised answer has not
reported
Dosimetry: mean heart dose in the 0.5 Gy range without the
internal mammary chain and 2.6 Gy with it (the lowest of any
technique); a 70-patient prospective series measured 0.44 Gy to
the whole heart.
The randomised RADCOMP trial has completed accrual (1,238
patients) with major cardiovascular events as its primary
endpoint, and has not reported — the registry's estimated
primary completion date is November 2036.
Protons carry their own costs: rib fracture in 7% of a
prospective cohort, and 3.7% at 3 years in a 225-patient series
(0.4% symptomatic); there is no photon skin-sparing effect at
the entrance, so skin dose depends on the planning.
Taiwan's three NHI proton codes (effective January 2026) all
apply only to patients under nineteen; proton therapy for adult
breast cancer is entirely self-paid.
DIBH
vertical axis: layers onto any photon technique
Not a machine — the posture you hold while the
beam is on
It layers onto 3D conformal, IMRT, VMAT or TOMO alike — which
is a separate question from which machine delivers the dose.
Reduction of roughly 20 to 70%, varying from person to person
(dosimetric); after pre-selection and training, about three in
ten still cannot complete a breath-hold planning scan.
The proton cell is the exception: mean heart dose with protons
under free breathing is already 0.48 Gy and falls to 0.31 Gy
with breath hold — the marginal gain is small.
The NHI schedule contains no respiratory-control or breath-hold
item, and no official published self-pay charge for photon
breath hold was found at any hospital — ask the business office.
Side is not the only axis: mean heart dose averages 5.4 Gy on the left and
3.3 Gy on the right, and including the internal mammary chain doubles the
typical heart dose — so a right-sided patient having the chain treated
needs the heart looked at too.
Schematic, redrawn from Taylor 2015, Drost 2018, Trivedi 2020, Pignol 2008,
Donovan 2007, Mukesh 2013, Lin 2021, Mutter 2021 (PTCOG consensus), the RADCOMP
trial registry and Taiwan's NHI fee schedule
Cohorts, designs and endpoints differ between studies; figures are not directly
comparable across cells
